pamphlet_excerpts: Pack Weighs Depends: How much your pack weighs depends on the length of the adventureyou have planned, the amount of food and equipment you must carry, and your personal.
Comfort Trail Pack: For comfort on the trail, a pack containing everything you need for a safe trek should tip the scale at no morethan 25 percent of your body’s weight.
Pack Weighs Here: If your pack weighs more, here are some tips for lighteningyour pack without compromising your health or safety. 1.
Shakedown Trip Shake: Do a shakedown before every trip to “shake out” everything youwon’t need. 2.
step_by_step_procedure: Divide Group Gear: Divide group gear so that each person carries a fair share. 3.
Gradually Replace Heavy: Gradually replace your heavy equipment and clothing with lighteritems.
Choose Lightweight Hiking: Choose lightweight hiking boots over stiff, heavy footwear. 5.
Prepare One-pot Meals: Prepare one-pot meals featuring pasta, powdered sauce mixes, andother ingredients that are dry, easy to pack, and not very heavy. 6.

pamphlet_excerpts: Extending Courtesy Outdoor: Extending courtesy to other outdoor visitors is a natural habitof backpackers.
Carry Amobile Telephone: If you carry amobile telephone for emergency communication, turn it off andstow it in your pack until you need it.
Appreciate Companyof Meet: Appreciate the companyof those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, butrespect their desire for quiet and solitude.
Encounter Horsebackriders: If you encounter horsebackriders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider what youshould do.
step_by_step_procedure: Lead Rider Probably: The lead rider will probably ask you to step a fewpaces downhill from the trail and stand quietly while theanimals pass.
Encounter Hikers: If you encounter other hikers or backpackersgoing uphill when you are going downhill, give them the rightof-way.
Aside Rock Log: Step aside on a rock or a log to minimize your impact.
Possible Campaway Trailsand: If possible, campaway from trailsand other visitors.

pamphlet_excerpts: Follow Guidelines Safe: Follow these guidelines for the safe use of chemical-fuel stoves. 1.
Compressed- Liquid-gas: Use compressed- or liquid-gas stoves only with knowledgeable adultsupervision and only where and when permitted.
Home Store Fuelcontainers: At home, store fuelcontainers in a shed, garage, or other uninhabited structure. 2.
Read Understand Manufacturer: Read and understand the manufacturer’s instructions before lightingany stove.
step_by_step_procedure: Liquid Fuels Well-marked: Keep liquid fuels in well-marked, approved containers only and neverin a glass container.
Store Fuel Ventilated: Store fuel in a ventilated, locked box a minimumof 20 feet from buildings and tents.
Chemical-fuel Containersaway: Keep all chemical-fuel containersaway from stoves and campfires and store them below 100 degrees. 4.
Stove Cool Completely: Let a stove cool completely before changing cylinders of compressedgases, refilling from containers of liquid gas, and storing the stove.

Appreciate Companyof Meet: Appreciate the companyof those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, butrespect their desire for quiet and solitude.
Encounter Horsebackriders: If you encounter horsebackriders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider what youshould do.
step_by_step_procedure: Lead Rider Probably: The lead rider will probably ask you to step a fewpaces downhill from the trail and stand quietly while theanimals pass.
Encounter Hikers: If you encounter other hikers or backpackersgoing uphill when you are going downhill, give them the rightof-way.
Aside Rock Log: Step aside on a rock or a log to minimize your impact.
Possible Campaway Trailsand: If possible, campaway from trailsand other visitors.
